project: Studio — a Phaser 4 game studio you can orchestrate

entries.title: Phaser 4 migration spike with AI-eval harness
entries.what: Stood up spike/ on Phaser 4.1.0: a deterministic 1/60 stepper, a generic 0-death autopilot, and a headless readback that is non-black on BOTH WebGL and Canvas.
entries.why: Prove Phaser 4 is AI-evaluable headless before committing — notably WebGL readback works in PH4 (PH3 forced the Canvas renderer here).

entries.title: Studio SDK + Phaser 4 game-template (0-death gate green)
entries.what: Wrote sdk/studio.js — the opinionated layer over Phaser 4 (harness, Autopilot, Level, Textures, Juice, Audio, Cam, Materials) — and a neutral game-template that passes the 0-death gate on both renderers.
entries.why: Make the studio conventions native so every scaffolded game inherits the eval backbone + feel surface instead of hand-rolling Phaser.

entries.title: Ship game-template to Railway (live) + deploy metadata
entries.what: Deployed the game-template from its own directory (railway up); verified /health + /api/meta and confirmed the live build renders headless.
entries.why: Close the loop end-to-end — a scaffolded base must be one push from a live URL.

entries.title: Studio conductor + vertical registry + orchestration docs
entries.what: Added orchestrator/: verticals.json (11 agent verticals, each wielding specific Phaser systems + a machine gate) and conductor.mjs, which runs the gate, reads GAME_META.stages, and emits the next agent brief in dependency order.
entries.why: Level up the PROCESS — turn the implicit 'build a game' method into an explicit, agent-orchestrated assembly line.

entries.title: Ember Depths — gate-green Phaser 4 showcase game
entries.what: Scaffolded games/ember from the template and drove it to a gate-green lava-cave platformer that exercises the Phaser-4 GPU FX + particle surfaces the older PH3 games never touched.
entries.why: Demonstrate the vertical agents by building a SECOND game that reuses the bottom of the stack and replaces the top.

entries.title: Ship Ember Depths to Railway (live)
entries.what: Deployed Ember Depths to its own Railway project; verified /health + /api/meta and a headless render of the live build.
entries.why: Ship the showcase game so the studio has a second live title proving the pipeline.

entries.title: Upgrade procedural art: shaded sprites, gradient ground, parallax backdrops
entries.what: Improved Studio.Textures (shaded, outlined sprites; vertical-gradient ground slabs) and added Studio.Backdrop (gradient sky pinned to camera + parallax silhouette layers).
entries.why: Instant depth and a cohesive look with no external art — procedural by construction.

entries.title: Ember Depths: real AI art via Gemini pipeline + headless 0-death gate
entries.what: Built the art pipeline in tools/art/ (Gemini image gen + chroma-key) to produce Ember's hero/enemy/ground/backdrop, kept the deterministic 0-death gate green.
entries.why: Show the Content tier's AI-art path while preserving the eval invariant (art is inert to the gate).

entries.title: Ember: themed floor/elements + on-screen joystick for mobile
entries.what: Themed the cave floor + elements via the Materials palette and added Studio.Touch — a multi-touch analog joystick + jump button for mobile.
entries.why: A live showcase needs to be playable on a phone, and the world needs to read as one place.

entries.title: Platformer feel (Studio.Platformer) + measured-fun (Studio.Feel) + conductor gate+feel
entries.what: Added Studio.Platformer (deterministic coyote/buffer/variable-jump/asymmetric-gravity controller) and Studio.Feel (a pure 4-component FUN predictor); wired feel into the conductor as a soft metric alongside the gate.
entries.why: Carry the proven jazz game-feel into the SDK and give the conductor a measurable fun signal to steer the next step.

entries.title: Ember 5-level campaign — measured FUN 43.2 -> 91.6, gate GREEN
entries.what: Rebuilt Ember's 2 flat levels into a 5-level descent authored straight to Studio.Feel (introduce -> develop -> twist -> master), each level peaking ~84% with varied beats and flow=1.0; mean FUN rose 43.2 -> 91.6.
entries.why: The original levels had dead-air windows; the fun model + reachability constraints drove a measurably better, still 0-death campaign.

entries.title: Contraptions: kinematic Studio.Contraptions + feeling dictionary + Matter spike
entries.what: Added Studio.Contraptions — a registry of deterministic kinematic machines (seesaw / launcher / crumble), each carrying a feeling + design lens + interest weight that Studio.Feel reads; plus spike-matter/ testing whether Phaser-4 Matter is deterministic under the fixed stepper.
entries.why: Layer emotional 'feeling' over a level without ever becoming a forced precision wall — and confirm arcade (not Matter) keeps the gate bit-identical.

entries.title: Contraption playground + Gemini AI-assist tool
entries.what: Built tools/contraptions/ — a standalone live playground (a scripted tester walks each machine) + a headless check.mjs verifier + a Gemini gen.mjs that turns plain English into a valid contraption spec pinned to the registry.
entries.why: Make contraptions designable and felt-out in isolation, with a verifier that proves each type actually moves and the canvas renders.

entries.title: Fullscreen: Phaser Scale.FIT + CENTER_BOTH (ember + template)
entries.what: Switched both ember and the game-template to Phaser Scale.FIT + CENTER_BOTH so the canvas fills the viewport and stays centered across aspect ratios.
entries.why: A deployed showcase should fill the screen on any device without distorting the fixed 960x540 world.

entries.title: Animate Ember hero: idle/run/jump sprite sheet + Phaser anims
entries.what: Generated an idle/run/jump sprite sheet for Ember's hero and wired Phaser animations; validate-anim.mjs proves the follower is a sprite whose rendered pixels differ frame-to-frame while the gate stays green.
entries.why: A live hero needs to read as animated, not a frozen image — without disturbing the deterministic gate.

entries.title: Sprite Studio: develop + animate + validate sprite animations
entries.what: Built tools/sprite-studio/ — a live Phaser anim bench + a Gemini gen.mjs (description -> chroma-keyed sheet) + a headless check.mjs that plays every anim, asserts it advances within range, and runs a structural + (optional) motion validator.
entries.why: Generalize the hero-animation work into a reusable, self-contained tool — the animation analogue of the contraption playground.

entries.title: Harden Sprite Studio gate (surfaced by running Ember's hero through it)
entries.what: Tightened the sprite-studio validator after feeding Ember's real hero sheet through it — closing gaps the bundled sample never exercised.
entries.why: A validator is only as good as the inputs it has seen; the real game asset exposed weak spots in the gate.

entries.title: Lego tool architecture: contract + registry + forge + dispatcher
entries.what: Formalized every tool as a gated 'brick': lego/contract.md (validate() is mandatory), registry.mjs (register() THROWS without a validator), forge.mjs (scaffolds from a template that already ships a validator), and dispatch.mjs (ensure-vendor -> run validator -> ACCEPT/REJECT). Seeded registry.json with the 3 forged + existing validators (sprite-animation, contraption, feel, gate, music).
entries.why: Make the invariant structural: a tool can only enter the assembly line if it is born gated — no 'register now, validate later'.

entries.title: Self-gating pipeline: art-cohesion + distinctness + sound validators, conductor --validate-all
entries.what: Forged/ported 3 judges as registry bricks (studio-art 9-dim cohesion, studio-distinct 6-axis uniqueness, studio-sound SFX wiring) and taught the conductor a --validate-all mode that runs EVERY game-applicable validator through the dispatcher into one scorecard.
entries.why: One command should answer "is this game good?" across every vertical — and the first full scorecard flagged a real problem (Ember art-cohesion 43.3 REJECT: placeholder tiles vs painterly backdrop).

entries.title: Sysmap deployed: the diary is a live, clickable system map
entries.what: Shipped the interactive visualizer to Railway behind a tiny no-dep static server (root redirects to /tools/sysmap/ so relative fetches of diary.json + registry.json resolve).
entries.why: A diagram you can open beats one you must build: every future diary entry/node appears on the live map on redeploy.
entries.validator: headless render check (45 nodes / 76 edges, zero console errors)

entries.title: texture-kit: the missing GENERATOR brick for the texturing capability
entries.what: Gap analysis against the scorecard found we could JUDGE art cohesion but not PRODUCE cohesive art. Forged texture-kit: Gemini generates material tiles (stone/mud/ice/lava) + pickups (coin/spring/goal) with the game's own backdrop as style-ref; a 2×2 mirror quilt makes every tile seamless BY CONSTRUCTION; the deterministic validator measures seams (<8/255), texture energy, palette affinity vs the backdrop (hue-histogram cosine), and sprite keying. Ember's kit: 19/19 checks, 100.
entries.why: The art-cohesion judge kept rejecting placeholder foreground tiles — the assembly line was missing the brick that closes that loop.

entries.title: Ember polish pass: 43.3 REJECT → 6/6 ACCEPT (art-cohesion 77.8)
entries.what: Integrated the kit per-material (mud/ice/stone finally read differently underfoot), switched to LINEAR filtering (pixelArt:true was shredding painterly tiles into pixel noise — the single biggest cohesion killer), added molten rim-lights on every slab, de-synced tile patterns per slab, themed the crumble ledge, hid the touch joystick on non-touch devices and themed it for touch, stroked-serif HUD + level title cards, per-depth backdrop tints, a proc:cave WebAudio ambience bed in the SDK (music 0.9→1.0), outlined the hero/enemy for silhouette, compound late climaxes on L1/L4 (FUN 90.4→90.5, L1 89→89.5), and a victory stop so the won hero no longer runs off the world edge.
entries.why: Make the flagship actually pass its own studio's full gate — quality measured, not asserted.
entries.validator: conductor --validate-all → 6/6 ACCEPT (gate ✓, feel 90.5, music 1.0, art-cohesion 77.8, distinctness 75, texturing 100)

entries.title: Real music: Lyria 2 composed loop replaces the inaudible synth bed
entries.what: The "music 1.0" score was hollow — the bed was a 55Hz procedural synth you could not hear, and the validator only checked a hook existed. Built tools/art/lyria.mjs: Google Lyria 2 (Vertex AI) generates a ~30s instrumental, downmixed to mono, peak-normalized, CROSSFADE-LOOPED into a seamless asset, MP3-encoded (~0.5MB) with a measured {rms,duration,model} sidecar. Ember loads assets/music/cave.mp3 on first gesture (proc synth kept only as offline fallback). Upgraded the music validator to VERIFY the bed: a referenced music file must exist and be provably non-silent or the gate FAILS.
entries.why: A passing score must mean what it says. "I can't hear any music" was correct — the gate could not tell silence from a song.
entries.validator: music (composed bed verified: lyria-002, 31.17s, rms 0.0456; playback proven in-browser)

entries.title: Playtest shell: pause + note-taking finally wired to the hub API
entries.what: Every game host has served the hub convention (/api/notes, /api/meta, /api/diary) since scaffold — but no game ever shipped the FRONT END. Built Studio.Shell (SDK): a DOM overlay with pause/resume (freezes the scene, ducks music), a 📝 note-taking panel that auto-pauses, releases the keyboard for typing, POSTs {text + where/level/x/coins/deaths} to /api/notes and lists the latest notes back, plus restart and mute (new Studio.Audio.setMuted reaches all registered beds). Wired into Ember AND the game-template so every future game inherits it.
entries.why: Playtesting needs margins to write in: a note pinned to the exact depth/position it was felt at is the studio's feedback loop closing.
entries.validator: browser proof: pause froze frame counter, note round-tripped through /api/notes with context, mute/restart verified; 0-death gate still GREEN (webgl+canvas)

entries.title: Sysmap: per-game lens + Flows (the order systems are called)
entries.what: The full map had become a 52-node hairball with no notion of sequence. Added (1) a LENS picker that filters the graph to one game's reachable subgraph (BFS over its depends-on/validated-by/feeds edges — "what does Ember actually use?"), and (2) FLOWS: a new optional diary.json section of curated, ordered walkthroughs the visualizer renders as numbered badges + an animated arrowed path with ◀ ▶ stepping and a per-step caption. Three flows shipped: the runtime frame loop (real update() order), the assembly-line vertical order, and the validate-all dispatch order. SCHEMA.md documents flows; gen-diary.mjs validates step refs and renders a Flows section into DIARY.md.
entries.why: A static edge set can answer "what connects to what" but never "in what order" — and per-game questions drowned in the all-systems view.
entries.validator: sysmap check.mjs extended: lensOk (ember subgraph strictly smaller, restores clean) + flowOk (badges == steps, stepping moves idx) — PASS; phone 390x844 verified no-overflow

entries.title: RFC-001: simplify the engine to one bundle, one CLI, data-only games, notes that feed back
entries.what: Architecture review with measurements: a new game owns 853 lines (only ~250 game-specific); studio.js exists in 5 copies (2 stale RIGHT NOW); 5 CLI entry points + 2 overlapping JSONs. Proposed four consolidations: (1) Studio.Game.boot(config) — games shrink to levels+theme+hooks (~80 lines); (2) build Studio INTO phaser-private as dist/phaser-studio.min.js with a stepMode engine flag (the deterministic stepper stops being a monkey-patch); (3) one `studio` CLI absorbing conductor/dispatch/forge/vendor, registry absorbing verticals, rules.json + a level-lint brick making the geometry contract data; (4) a notes-loop brick: pull /api/notes from every deployed game, Gemini-triage to capabilities, surface as backlog in `studio next`, credit closed notes in diary entries — play→note→triage→dispatch→gate→diary, the full circle.
entries.why: The essential loop is one sentence — clone a game, apply rules, call the right tool, forge when missing, gate everything — and the architecture should be the same size as the sentence. The deterministic gates make the refactor safe: 6/6 ACCEPT is the acceptance test for every migration step.
entries.validator: each migration step gated by conductor --validate-all staying 6/6 on ember + template

entries.title: RFC-001 implemented: Studio.Game.boot, studio CLI, rules.json + level-lint, notes-loop
entries.what: Executed the engine simplification. Studio.Game.boot(config) turns a game into data+theme+hooks (Ember's 513-line game.js → ~70-line config; one runtime owns world/theme/HUD/shell/autopilot/harness/win-death, runner + vertical archetypes). rules.json makes the geometry contract data; the forged level-lint brick gates levels statically before the browser gate. The studio CLI (new/next/run/lint/gate/feel/check/ship/notes) is the one front door; the registry absorbed verticals.json. The notes-loop brick (pull/triage) closes play→note→dispatch.
entries.why: The essential loop — clone, apply rules, call the right tool, gate — should be the size of that sentence. The deterministic gates made the rewrite safe (Ember held 6/6 throughout).
entries.validator: Ember --validate-all held ACCEPT across the port

entries.title: Nimbus Climb: a new vertical sky-climber proves the refactor (7/7 ACCEPT)
entries.what: Built a brand-new game in the clouds via boot({archetype:'vertical'}). New SDK verbs: updraft wind-columns (ride up, steer out), cloud/mist/crystal/storm materials, climb-axis Feel scoring, a waypoint-chain vertical autopilot. tools/level-gen/sky.mjs generates the 5 towers reachable-by-construction. Full Gemini art (painterly cloud backdrop, animated cloud-spirit hero) + Lyria sky music. Two validators were generalized beyond Ember's conventions in the process (music scans the vendored SDK for boot() games; texturing reads materials from theme-kit.json).
entries.why: A second, differently-shaped game is the real test of "clone a game, apply rules" — and it forced the engine + validators to become genuinely archetype-agnostic.
entries.validator: gate GREEN webgl+canvas, deterministic; --validate-all 7/7 ACCEPT (feel, gate, music 1.0, art 64.4, distinct 91.7, texturing 100, rules 100)

entries.title: Shell parity: deepfin-bar menus, save/progression, notes-SPACE fix, decorative vertical enemies
entries.what: Parity audit vs the reference games (deepfin screenshot as the quality bar) then filled engine-side: Studio.Menu (full-bleed backdrop, breathing hero art, generated WORDMARK lockup + tagline, zone rail of per-level thumbnail cards with locks + best coins/time, level-complete card, win screen, sound toggle — touch + keyboard) and Studio.Save (localStorage progression). New bricks: logo.mjs (Gemini wordmark per game) and menu-shots (auto-screenshots every level into its zone card via the additive __game.gotoLevel hook). Fixed the notes textarea swallowing SPACE (Phaser key CAPTURES preventDefault at the manager level — Shell now clears/restores captures). Nimbus regains visible storm-imps as decorative patrollers; interactive vertical enemies stay backlog after bisecting a sub-pixel landing race that diverged the gate.
entries.why: Every engine game should boot like a finished product — deepfin set the bar; the engine way is to pay that cost ONCE in the SDK + tools.
entries.validator: gates GREEN both games (nimbus double-gate 2426/2426 deterministic WITH enemies); menus verified live on both deploys

entries.title: Connected to the family: per-game repos, notes→ISSUES, hub registration, deepfin on the map
entries.what: Ember Depths + Nimbus Climb are standalone GitHub repos now (studio publish = subtree push; GAME_META.repo is truth). Playtest notes auto-file as GitHub issues (label playtest-note, note-id back-reference; the user's 5 rescued Nimbus notes became nimbus-climb#1–5, and a live test note became #6 end-to-end). Both games registered in game-engine hub/games.json (commit 6b952fa). Shell gained the deepfin corner links (DIARY / REPO / NOTES→ISSUES / ENGINE). The sysmap now shows the whole FAMILY: the hub + deepfin/jazz/the-platformer as sibling games, with the lineage edges (feel←jazz, menu←deepfin). Duplicate studio-sysmap Railway project deleted.
entries.why: A game is not shipped until it lives where the rest of the family lives: its own repo, its notes in issues, its card in the hub.
entries.validator: live POST /api/notes → nimbus-climb#6 created automatically; hub games.json lists 5 games; gates GREEN

entries.title: New archetype: vertical space shooter (Studio.Shooter) + Starlance, shipped
entries.what: Added a third archetype to the engine — a vertical space shooter — and built Starlance with it in one pass. Studio.Shooter is a distinct game loop (no gravity/platforms) that reuses the shared chrome (Shell/Save/Audio/Touch/harness/Menu-local). The deterministic 0-death problem for a shmup is solved by the SWEEPING-GAP BULLET CURTAIN: bullets rain in columns except a safe gap weaving on a fixed-dt clock; constants satisfy sweepSpeed·fallTime < gapW/2−shipHalf so the live gap is always a safe column the autopilot rides while auto-firing; formations are non-deadly score targets; the boss dies to sustained fire while the ship dodges. rules.json + level-lint encode the survivability bound as a checkable contract. Full Gemini art (ship, 3 enemies, mothership boss, powerup, 5 veil backdrops) + Lyria synthwave drive. Repo agadabanka/starlance (private), notes→issues server, registered in the hub (6 games), deployed.
entries.why: A genuinely different genre is the proof the engine is an engine, not a platformer — and the curtain shows the "AI-completable by construction" discipline generalises beyond running and climbing.
entries.validator: gate GREEN webgl+canvas, double-gate frame-identical (7875, score 3900, 0 deaths, boss destroyed); level-lint 100/100 (every veil provably survivable)

entries.title: Fourth archetype: car RTS (Studio.RTS) + Roadwar — and a design-lens tool
entries.what: Added a fourth archetype — a toon-shaded car RTS — and built Roadwar (5 grounds) with it. Studio.RTS is a deterministic 3-lane lane-push: spend auto-income SCRAP to BUILD cars (scout/brawler/gunner) that drive up and brawl; win = fortress HP→0, lose = garage HP→0. The 0-death problem is solved WIN-BY-CONSTRUCTION via two STATIC economic bounds (rules.json + level-lint), not geometry: ACCUMULATION (income/cost > fortressTurret.dmg/(cd·hp) so the all-in-rally deathball grows unbounded and the finite-schedule fortress falls) and SIDE-LEAK (a garage-HP budget on off-rally scouts the all-lane base gun clears). New tools this pass: a pure-Node econ sim that tunes balance in ms before the browser gate, and — following the platformer's design-lens path — `studio lens`, a DESIGN DIAGNOSTIC (MDA + Schell lenses) that traces each weak Feel component to the lens that asks why + a concrete mechanic fix. The lens drove FUN 65→86.3 through real design: a Warlord boss climax, per-ground signatures (introduce→develop→twist→master), intensity escalating 9→45 to the finale. Also hardened `studio publish` to CREATE the repo (private) if missing — every game IS a repo. Full Gemini toon art + Lyria anthem. Repo agadabanka/roadwar (private), notes→issues, hub (7 games), deployed.
entries.why: Two lessons made first-class. (1) A fourth genre on the SAME engine + autopilot — its win-by-construction expressed as ECONOMIC bounds rather than geometry — is more proof the engine generalizes past platformers. (2) 'Make it more fun' became a TOOL, not vibes: the design lens turns a low Feel number into the lens that asks why and the mechanic that fixes it, so fun rises by design (a boss, a ramp) and the score follows honestly.
entries.validator: gate GREEN webgl+canvas frame-identical (9801, 0 deaths, all 5 grounds, boss fought); level-lint rts 100% (accumulation + side-leak); FUN 86.3 (bar 80) via design-lens; deployed live

entries.title: Engine polish pass: economy, per-level music, richer juice/props, composite FUN — and the hub unstuck
entries.what: A round of ENGINE-LEVEL upgrades (every game inherits them), driven by playtest notes. (1) ECONOMY: a buildable REFINERY (coin generation) in Studio.RTS — spend scrap to raise income, the army-vs-economy choice; the autopilot opens with refineries (autoEcon) on the later grounds and still gates 0-death (8966, deterministic). (2) PER-LEVEL MUSIC: Studio.levelMusic + Audio.switchMusic cross-fade a distinct track per level across ALL three archetypes (theme.musicByLevel / levels[i].music); the music validator now verifies every per-level track and scores per-level variety. Roadwar ships 5 distinct Lyria battle themes (desert/junkyard/neon/canyon/boss-metal). (3) JUICE + PROPS: Studio.Juice gains explode / ring / muzzle / popText / ambient-drift, wired through RTS combat (hit rings, ranged muzzle flashes, scaled death explosions, a WARLORD-DOWN pop, a fortress-fall explosion chain) plus procedural roadside props + ground atmosphere. (4) COMPOSITE FUN: the design lens now also scores PRODUCTION POLISH (Schell #58 juice · #62 spectacle · #40 reward · #31 variety · #63 beauty) — the real fun the geometry Feel model is blind to — and blends it with the level-design score for the headline FUN (Roadwar 86.3 design + 100 polish = 91.5). (5) The game-engine HUB 'stuck on loading' bug was fixed (cold-start cache-poisoning in /api/dashboard) and starsweeper registered → all 8 games show.
entries.why: The throughline the playtests asked for: put the RULES in the ENGINE. Economy, per-level scores, juice and props aren't per-game hacks — they're SDK capabilities with validators, so the next game gets them free. And 'make it more fun' got a measurable home: the lens credits the production polish the Feel model couldn't see, so juice/spectacle/reward/variety/beauty count toward FUN by design, honestly.
entries.validator: gate 0-death webgl+canvas (8966); music validator per-level (5/5 tracks, perLevelMusic ✓); design-lens FUN 91.5 (design 86.3 + polish 100); hub /api/dashboard 8 games, no hang

entries.title: Isometric archetype (Studio.Iso + Studio.IsoRTS) + a strategy-sweep eval beyond 0-death
entries.what: Two building blocks. (1) ISOMETRIC: Studio.Iso is a reusable perspective-iso PROJECTOR (configure screen anchors once → project lx∈[-1,1] across + t∈[0,1] depth to a screen point with perspective scale + depth-sort; lxAt inverts a click) — the foundation for any future iso game of any genre. Studio.IsoRTS is a new archetype built on it: the car RTS on a FREER continuous-front battlefield (a continuous lateral lx, not 3 fixed lanes) drawn in 2.5D iso, REUSING the RTS economy + combat + win-by-construction (lane→lx band). Roadwar Iso ships with a full iso art set (5 backdrops + 10 sprites) and gates 0-death deterministically (9005). (2) A new KIND of eval: tools/eval/strategies.mjs sweeps 7 AI playstyles (brawler-ball, scout-swarm, gunner-line, eco-boom, no-eco, mixed-arms, spread-front) through every ground and reports strategic DIVERSITY (how many styles win = meaningful choices, Schell #32), TENSION (how close the garage came — stomp vs nail-biter) and a per-ground challenge profile. It immediately exposed what the binary 0-death gate hides: the grounds are STOMPS (every style wins, tension ≈ 0).
entries.why: Per playtest steer: 0-death is one optimal strategy's yes/no — a weak signal. The richer questions are 'is it a stomp?' and 'does more than one strategy work?'. The strategy sweep + the fun-maximizer (design lens) are the new quality bar; 0-death becomes a sanity floor, not the goal. And the iso projector + archetype are engine building blocks, so the next iso/RTS game inherits them.
entries.validator: iso gate 0-death webgl+canvas (9005, frame-identical); strategy-sweep 7×5; design-lens FUN 91.7

nodes.label: Foundations
nodes.desc: The base — the method + the working game/skeleton. Inherited whole, never rebuilt.

nodes.label: Platform
nodes.desc: The shared rig: the always-on services every feature leans on (server, persistence, Gemini/Lyria, Railway deploy).

nodes.label: Engine
nodes.desc: Phaser 4, AI-first: scenes, the materials/element model, controls, the level DSL.

nodes.label: Content
nodes.desc: Where worlds + assets come from: the art pipeline, the texture bakery, juice, audio, the authoring tools.

nodes.label: Evaluation
nodes.desc: The AI playtester: the 0-death gate, the felt-fun score, the per-tool validators, the Lego gate.

nodes.label: Feedback
nodes.desc: From 'I felt something' to a fix: the conductor, the vertical registry, the build diary.

nodes.label: Publish
nodes.desc: The deployed games — a push to main auto-deploys the live build on Railway.

nodes.label: the-harness (method)
nodes.desc: Build levels as stories; make an AI beat each at 0 deaths before it ships; score the fun; record the proof.

nodes.label: Phaser 4 spike
nodes.desc: spike/ — proves PH4 is AI-evaluable headless: deterministic stepper + 0-death gate + non-black WebGL & Canvas readback.

nodes.label: Matter determinism spike
nodes.desc: spike-matter/ — is Phaser-4 Matter deterministic under the fixed stepper? (answer: arcade stays bit-identical; Matter does not).

nodes.label: Railway deploy
nodes.desc: Per-game Railway project; railway up from the game dir; /health + /api/meta + headless render verify the live build.

nodes.label: Art pipeline (Gemini)
nodes.desc: tools/art/ — Gemini image gen + chroma-key; model-sheet-conditioned hero/enemy/ground/backdrop. Degrades to procedural offline.

nodes.label: Studio SDK
nodes.desc: sdk/studio.js — the opinionated layer over Phaser 4 that makes the studio conventions native (the umbrella for the modules below).

nodes.label: Studio.harness
nodes.desc: Deterministic 1/60 stepper (window.__rec) + semantic observability (window.__game) + __run/__gate. The eval contract.

nodes.label: Studio.Autopilot
nodes.desc: Generic platformer driver (the 0-death gate policy) + ground probes; holds jump through the ascent for full height.

nodes.label: Studio.Level
nodes.desc: Data-driven level DSL -> built world; one wide static body per slab (no seam-catching), with springs/movers/contraptions.

nodes.label: Studio.Materials
nodes.desc: Each surface declares look + footing + machine-readable grounding, so levels are AI-completable by construction.

nodes.label: Studio.Platformer
nodes.desc: Deterministic movement controller: coyote time, jump buffer, variable jump, asymmetric gravity, run-accel/skid.

nodes.label: Studio.Contraptions
nodes.desc: Registry of kinematic machines (seesaw/launcher/crumble), each with a feeling + design lens + interest weight; autopilot-safe flair.

nodes.label: Studio.Cam
nodes.desc: Follow camera with deadzone + bounds.

nodes.label: Studio.Touch
nodes.desc: On-screen multi-touch analog joystick + jump button for mobile.

nodes.label: Studio.Textures
nodes.desc: Procedural texture bakery — shaded/outlined sprites, gradient ground slabs, contraption art; no external art required.

nodes.label: Studio.Backdrop
nodes.desc: Gradient sky pinned to camera + parallax silhouette layers — instant depth.

nodes.label: Studio.Juice
nodes.desc: The feel surface: tweens, particles, Phaser-4 GPU filters (glow/vignette/ColorMatrix), shake, hit-stop. Inert-until-fired.

nodes.label: Studio.Audio
nodes.desc: Procedural WebAudio SFX (jump/coin/stomp/hurt/win) + a music hook.

nodes.label: Studio.Feel
nodes.desc: Pure deterministic FUN predictor from level placement: 0.35*engagement + 0.15*dynamics + 0.25*arc + 0.25*flow.

nodes.label: 0-death gate
nodes.desc: The ship bar: determinism (two identical runs) + 0-death autopilot + non-black readback, per renderer (webgl & canvas).

nodes.label: eval-feel (feel.mjs)
nodes.desc: tools/eval/feel.mjs — serves a game's src/, scores every level via the in-page Studio.Feel; soft metric (always exits 0).

nodes.label: game-gate (eval.mjs)
nodes.desc: The per-game eval.mjs brick: the registry capability that runs the 0-death gate against a --game dir.

nodes.label: sprite-animation gate
nodes.desc: sprite-studio's check.mjs: zero page errors + every anim advances in range + structural (+ optional Gemini motion).

nodes.label: contraption gate
nodes.desc: contraptions' check.mjs: cycles every registry type, asserts it moves, non-black readback.

nodes.label: music gate
nodes.desc: studio-sound's validate.mjs — the registered gate for the music capability.

nodes.label: The Tool Contract
nodes.desc: lego/contract.md — every tool is a brick: manifest + run + REQUIRED validate(); a tool is registerable only if it has a validator.

nodes.label: Lego registry
nodes.desc: lego/registry.mjs + registry.json — the executable index of bricks; register() THROWS without a validator (the invariant lives here).

nodes.label: Lego forge
nodes.desc: lego/forge.mjs — scaffolds a new brick from a template that already ships a validator, then registers it (so it is born gated).

nodes.label: Lego dispatcher
nodes.desc: lego/dispatch.mjs — the root accept/reject gate: ensure-vendor -> run the brick's validator -> ACCEPT/REJECT (exit code composes).

nodes.label: Sprite Studio
nodes.desc: tools/sprite-studio/ — develop + animate + validate sprite animations: live bench + Gemini gen + headless check.

nodes.label: Contraption Playground
nodes.desc: tools/contraptions/ — live playground (a tester walks each machine) + Gemini gen + headless check.

nodes.label: Studio Sound
nodes.desc: tools/studio-sound/ — the music brick (forged from the template; gated by validate.mjs).

nodes.label: Conductor
nodes.desc: orchestrator/conductor.mjs — runs the gate, reads GAME_META.stages, picks the next ready vertical, emits its agent brief; folds in feel.

nodes.label: Vertical registry
nodes.desc: orchestrator/verticals.json — 11 agent verticals in dependency order, each with the Phaser systems it wields + a machine gate.

nodes.label: ORCHESTRATION.md
nodes.desc: The studio's north star: level up the engine (SDK on PH4) + level up the process (verticals become agents; hub becomes conductor).

nodes.label: Game Template
nodes.desc: game-template/ — the neutral Phaser 4 base on the Studio SDK; the canonical clean game new titles are scaffolded from. Live on Railway.

nodes.label: Ember Depths
nodes.desc: games/ember/ — a 5-level lava-cave platformer showing off the PH4 GPU FX + particles; mean FUN 91.6, gate green. Live on Railway.

nodes.label: Ember campaign (levels.js)
nodes.desc: games/ember/src/game/levels.js — the 5-level descent authored to Studio.Feel (introduce -> develop -> twist -> master).

nodes.label: Studio Art (cohesion judge)
nodes.desc: tools/studio-art/ — screenshots a game headless and scores 9-dim VISUAL COHESION 0-100 with Gemini vision (threshold 60).

nodes.label: Studio Distinct (uniqueness judge)
nodes.desc: tools/studio-distinct/ — scores a game's UNIQUENESS vs a sibling or the stock-platformer baseline (Gemini vision, 6 axes).

nodes.label: Studio Diary (diary.json)
nodes.desc: diary/SCHEMA.md + diary.json — the machine-readable build log + systems graph; DIARY.md is a render, the sysmap consumes it directly.

nodes.label: Sysmap (interactive visualizer)
nodes.desc: tools/sysmap/ — vanilla JS+SVG force-graph of diary.json + registry.json; deployed at studio-sysmap-production.up.railway.app.

nodes.label: Texture Kit (style-matched tiles)
nodes.desc: tools/texture-kit/ — generates a SEAMLESS material tile kit + themed sprites from the game's own backdrop as Gemini style-ref (2×2 mirror quilt); deterministic validator: seam/energy/palette-affinity/alpha.

nodes.label: Lyria Music (Vertex)
nodes.desc: tools/art/lyria.mjs — generates a real instrumental loop with Google Lyria 2 (Vertex AI), downmixes + crossfade-loops + MP3-encodes, writes a measured sidecar so the music validator can prove it is non-silent.

nodes.label: Playtest Shell
nodes.desc: Studio.Shell — DOM playtest overlay every game inherits: pause/resume (scene + music duck), 📝 notes POSTing {text + live game context} to the host's /api/notes, restart, mute. Inert until clicked, so the deterministic gate is untouched.

nodes.label: RFC-001 Engine Simplification
nodes.desc: rfc/001-engine-simplification.md — one bundle (phaser-studio.min.js built by the fork), one CLI front door, games as data+hooks via Studio.Game.boot, rules.json as first-class data, and a notes-loop brick so every playtest note feeds the next dispatch.

nodes.label: studio CLI
nodes.desc: studio.mjs — one front door: new/next/run/lint/gate/feel/check/ship/notes; wraps conductor+dispatch+forge.

nodes.label: Studio.Game.boot
nodes.desc: the declarative game runtime: a game is data + theme tokens + hooks; all per-game glue (world/theme/HUD/shell/autopilot/harness/win-death) is one SDK impl. runner + vertical archetypes.

nodes.label: rules.json + level-lint
nodes.desc: the geometry contract as data (per archetype) + the cheap static gate that lints levels before the browser gate.

nodes.label: notes-loop
nodes.desc: tools/notes-loop — pull /api/notes from every deployed game, Gemini-triage to capabilities; closes play→note→dispatch→diary.

nodes.label: sky level-gen
nodes.desc: tools/level-gen/sky.mjs — generates vertical towers reachable-by-construction (staggered lanes, centre-column updrafts, storm framing).

nodes.label: Nimbus Climb
nodes.desc: the cloud sky-climber (vertical archetype): updraft riding, storm walls, 5 towers. Built as a ~60-line boot() config. 7/7 validators ACCEPT.

nodes.label: Studio.Menu + Save
nodes.desc: deepfin-bar menu inside boot(): full-bleed backdrop, breathing hero, generated wordmark lockup, zone rail of per-level thumbnail cards (lock/best), level-complete card, win screen; Studio.Save persists unlocked+best. Eval-safe: harness reset() bypasses.

nodes.label: logo + menu-shots
nodes.desc: tools/art/logo.mjs (Gemini wordmark per game, keyed) + tools/menu-shots (screenshots every level via __game.gotoLevel into zone cards that can never drift).

nodes.label: game-engine hub
nodes.desc: agadabanka/game-engine — the family hub: hub/games.json registers every shipped game (repo/url/meta/stages); notes→issues convention; the studio's games are registered there too.

nodes.label: Deepfin
nodes.desc: agadabanka/deepfin — Pearl the axolotl swims five fathoms (built on game-engine). Its menu lockup + notes→issues protocol set the quality bar the studio now matches.

nodes.label: Jazz
nodes.desc: agadabanka/jazz — the bunny-with-a-bazooka platformer whose movement tune + FUN model the studio ported.

nodes.label: the-platformer
nodes.desc: agadabanka/the-platformer — the base game + rig the whole family was built from.

nodes.label: Studio.Shooter
nodes.desc: the vertical space-shooter archetype: a separate game loop reusing Shell/Save/Audio/Touch/harness; the sweeping-gap bullet curtain is 0-death-by-construction (sweepSpeed·fallTime < gapW/2 − shipHalf).

nodes.label: Starlance
nodes.desc: agadabanka/starlance — a vertical space shooter: 5 nebula veils to the Hollow Star mothership boss. Full Gemini art + Lyria drive. Built as a ~30-line shooter boot() config; gate GREEN 0-death deterministic.

nodes.label: Studio.RTS
nodes.desc: The car-RTS archetype: deterministic 3-lane lane-push (build→rally→brawl). Win-by-construction via economic bounds (accumulation + side-leak), not geometry.

nodes.label: Design Lens
nodes.desc: MDA + Jesse Schell's lenses as a tool: traces each weak Feel component to the lens that asks why + a concrete per-archetype mechanic fix; judges per-level quality AND campaign intensity escalation.

nodes.label: Roadwar
nodes.desc: A toon-shaded car RTS — 5 grounds, a Warlord boss finale; built on Studio.RTS, tuned through the design lens.

nodes.label: Studio.Iso
nodes.desc: Reusable perspective-iso projector: lx+depth → screen with perspective scale + depth-sort. The building block behind any isometric game.

nodes.label: Studio.IsoRTS
nodes.desc: Isometric continuous-front RTS archetype (built on Studio.Iso); reuses the RTS economy/combat/win-by-construction with lane→lx band.

nodes.label: Roadwar Iso
nodes.desc: The isometric 2.5D redesign of the car RTS — a freer continuous-front battlefield.

nodes.label: Strategy Sweep
nodes.desc: Runs many AI playstyles through a level → strategic diversity + tension + balance. A different kind of eval than the binary 0-death gate.

flows.title: Runtime: one Ember frame
flows.desc: What actually runs, in order, every 1/60s step of Ember Depths (game.js update()).

steps.label: step
steps.note: game.step(t, dt) — the deterministic stepper drives update(); same dt every frame, so runs replay bit-identically.

steps.label: world tick
steps.note: movers + contraptions advance on the deterministic phase clock; the interaction pass may launch (geyser) or arm a collapse (crumble).

steps.label: input
steps.note: read the player: keyboard + the on-screen joystick/JUMP (touch devices).

steps.label: or autopilot
steps.note: in eval runs the autopilot senses ground/walls/enemies ahead and emits the decision instead.

steps.label: footing
steps.note: probe the slab under the feet — ice is slick, mud is sticky; friction feeds the controller.

steps.label: movement
steps.note: Studio.Platformer applies coyote time, jump buffer, variable jump, asymmetric gravity, skid.

steps.label: feel & FX
steps.note: state-driven hero anims, landing shake, ember bursts, glow/grade — visual only, never touches physics.

steps.label: camera
steps.note: deadzone follow pans the cave after movement settles.

steps.label: sound
steps.note: event SFX (jump/coin/stomp/win) + the Lyria cave loop under it all.

steps.label: shell
steps.note: outside the loop: the playtest shell can pause the whole scene or pin a note to this exact frame.

flows.title: Assembly line: how a game gets built
flows.desc: The conductor drives the verticals in this order; each stage is gated before the next.

steps.label: conductor
steps.note: reads GAME_META.stages and prints the next vertical's brief — the studio's showrunner.

steps.label: story/concept
steps.note: Writers' Room + Showrunner briefs set the fiction and the verbs.

steps.label: art theme
steps.note: the painterly backdrop locks the palette every later asset must match.

steps.label: characters
steps.note: Gemini hero/enemy sheets, chroma-keyed + sliced on-model.

steps.label: level design
steps.note: the campaign in the Level DSL — geometry rules keep every level AI-completable.

steps.label: gameplay
steps.note: Studio.Feel scores FUN per level; beats are tuned to the interest curve.

steps.label: animation
steps.note: animate the hero and run the sheet through the sprite gate.

steps.label: texturing
steps.note: style-matched seamless tile kit generated from the backdrop itself.

steps.label: sound
steps.note: Lyria 2 composes the loop; SFX wired to every key event.

steps.label: QA gate
steps.note: the 0-death deterministic autopilot run, webgl + canvas.

steps.label: ship
steps.note: railway up — the game gets a live URL.

flows.title: Quality gate: conductor --validate-all
flows.desc: One command answers "is this game good?" — every registered validator runs through the dispatcher into a scorecard (Ember: 6/6 ACCEPT).

steps.label: collect
steps.note: gathers every game-applicable capability from the registry.

steps.label: registry
steps.note: the Lego index — register() refuses any brick without a validator.

steps.label: dispatch
steps.note: runs each brick's validator, captures the JSON verdicts.

steps.label: gate
steps.note: 0-death deterministic run on both renderers.

steps.label: feel
steps.note: FUN model on the level specs (Ember 90.5).

steps.label: music
steps.note: SFX wiring + the bed must be provably non-silent (Lyria sidecar).

steps.label: art-cohesion
steps.note: Gemini vision, 9 dimensions, threshold 60 (Ember 73.9–77.8).

steps.label: distinctness
steps.note: uniqueness vs the stock-platformer baseline (Ember 86.7).

steps.label: texturing
steps.note: seams, texture energy, palette affinity vs the backdrop (19/19) → scorecard verdict back at the conductor.

flows.title: Runtime: one Roadwar frame
flows.desc: What runs every 1/60s step of Roadwar (Studio.RTS update()) — deterministic, so eval replays bit-identically.

steps.label: step
steps.note: game.step(t, dt) drives update() with the same dt every frame.

steps.label: build (rally)
steps.note: in eval the all-in-rally macro builds autoBuild on the rally lane whenever scrap allows — the win-by-construction strategy.

steps.label: tickWorld
steps.note: scrap += income·dt; units (id-order) seek the nearest enemy ahead in-lane, hold at engage range, fight on cd, else advance or hit the HQ; HQ turrets defend all lanes; the finite enemy schedule spawns on the clock.

steps.label: win/lose
steps.note: fortressHp≤0 → next ground / won; garageHp≤0 → death. Deterministic, no RNG.

steps.label: (offline) score
steps.note: Studio.Feel reads the schedule as a rising battle-heat curve; the design lens turns weak components into mechanic fixes.
